[hitman86] I asked Chatgpt and it helped me compare this with the Optimum Nutrition 100% Whey I'm currently using
TLDR; this Musashi is not worth the extra calories for most use cases :
Your ON powder is therefore roughly three-quarters protein by weight, whereas the Musashi is less than half protein by weight.
The ingredient lists explain why. Your Gold Standard starts with whey protein isolate, whey protein concentrate and whey peptides. The Musashi starts with a milk-protein blend—primarily WPC, skim milk powder, whole milk powder and WPI—but then adds maltodextrin and dextrose, which are rapidly digested carbohydrates.
So if you drink one serving after your workout, the comparison is basically:
Gold Standard:
24 g protein + 3 g carbs for 119 calories.
Musashi Bulk:
26 g protein + ~24 g carbs for ~229 calories.
You're consuming almost twice the calories for only ~2 g more protein with the Musashi.
For your situation, I would stick with the Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard. Your aim is to support your strength training and muscle development, rather than deliberately trying to put on a lot of body mass. The extra maltodextrin, dextrose and calories in the Musashi aren't inherently “bad”, but there's no particular reason for you to pay for and consume them simply to get your post-workout protein.
There is one important distinction, though: if you told me “I'm struggling to eat enough, I'm losing weight, and I specifically want to gain several kilos”, then the Musashi starts making sense. That's what this product is designed for.
Also, the Good Price Pharmacy price showing for that 2 kg Musashi is currently $66.74, which makes it look exceptionally cheap. But because nearly half the tub is carbohydrate rather than protein, comparing it to whey purely on $/kg of powder is misleading.
